text_blocks.snippet: Current scam trends targeting Central Illinois include fraudulent garage door repair schemes, fake DMV text messages, and deceptive online shopping or delivery notifications.
Active Scam Trends in Central Illinois

list.snippet: Garage Door Repair Cons: Scammers use search engines to pose as legitimate local businesses (such as The Door Doctor or Crawford and Brinkman), install cheap generic parts, overcharge drastically, or intentionally sabotage cables to manufacture fake emergencies.

Fake DMV / Tollway Texts: Residents across Illinois receive fraudulent text messages claiming to be from the Illinois Secretary of State or tollway system, falsely alleging unpaid fines or impending license suspensions to steal financial data.
Package and Delivery Smishing: Scammers send text messages pretending to be USPS or UPS claiming a package delivery failed due to address errors, urging users to click malicious links.
AI and Impersonation Scams: The Better Business Bureau of Central Illinois warns of an increase in AI-driven family/celebrity impersonations, tech support traps, and fake relationship/romance fraud.
Verify the Source: Never click links in unexpected text messages or emails regarding tolls, DMV violations, or package deliveries. The Secretary of State never requests payment via text.
Inspect Contractors: Check for branded company uniforms, verified physical addresses, and proper local licensing before agreeing to home or garage repairs.
Practice the Pause: Slow down during urgent requests for money or personal data, and independently look up the official phone number to verify claims.
